description: Update a saved popup: rename it, publish or unpublish it via status, retarget its audience, change when and where it fires, edit its copy, restyle its theme, or replace its content blocks. Read the current content via get_popup first when editing blocks. Setting status to draft stops it showing without deleting it or changing the embed script.

blocks.description: Full replacement for the popup's content blocks. Fetch the current blocks from get_popup, modify them, and send the complete array - the popup must keep exactly one required email field and one submit button. Blocks render in array order; every block needs a globally unique "id" and a "kind", and "sectionId" ("success" or "error") moves a content block into that screen. Layout groups use { id, kind: "group", label, layout: "stack" | "row" | "grid" | "overlay", columns (1-4), gap (0-64), padding (0-64), overlayColor (hex), overlayPosition ("top" | "center" | "bottom"), overlayShade (0-100), children: [...] }. In Overlay, gap spaces foreground children while the direct image remains the background. Overlay needs exactly one direct image; images inside subgroups only enable Overlay for that subgroup, while zero or multiple direct images fall back to Stack. Groups may nest to three levels; descendants must use the same sectionId as their group, while form-step, success-screen, and error-state remain at the root. Input blocks are kind "form-field": { id, kind: "form-field", fieldType, name, label, placeholder, required, defaultValue, showLabel, width ("full" | "half"), mapsTo, options }. fieldType is one of text, email, phone, number, textarea, select, radio, checkbox, consent, hidden. mapsTo is one of email, firstName, lastName, phone, customAttribute and defaults to customAttribute, which stores the answer under the block's "name" as a subscriber custom attribute. select, radio, and checkbox fields require options: [{ value, label, id }] - label and id default to value when omitted. Other kinds and their properties: heading { content, level (1-3), align }, text { content, variant ("paragraph" | "eyebrow" | "caption"), align }, image { src, alt, fit ("cover" | "contain") }, button { text, url, variant, align }, divider {}, spacer { height (8-160) }, custom-html { html, height (40-1200) } - the markup goes in "html", not "content" - feature-grid { features: [{ title, description }], columns }, testimonial { testimonials: [{ quote, name, role }] }, countdown { label, endsAt }, form-step { title, description, blockIds }, submit-button { text, width }, success-screen { heading, message }, error-state { message }. Properties outside a kind's list are rejected rather than dropped, so a typo is reported instead of silently saving an empty block. Validation errors name the offending property, for example "blocks[3].children[0].options[0].value".

botProtection.description: Turn on a Cloudflare Turnstile bot check before each signup. It runs invisibly for most visitors; signups that fail it must confirm by email before they are subscribed; turning it on requires a double opt-in confirmation email and a sender profile, otherwise the API returns 400. Omit to keep the current setting.

companyId.description: Company ID. If not provided, uses the currently selected company.

description.description: New text for the popup's first paragraph block. Fails if the popup has no paragraph block; edit blocks instead.

duplicateStrategy.description: How to handle an existing subscriber.

frequency.description: How often one visitor sees it: { "maxDisplays": 1-100, "windowDays": 1-365 }. Merged into the current frequency.

headline.description: New text for the popup's first heading block. Fails if the popup has no heading block; edit blocks instead.

listIds.description: Replacement list targeting. Pass an empty array to capture into every list.

placement.description: Where the popup sits in the viewport.

popupId.description: Saved popup ID returned by list_popups or create_popup.

presentation.description: How the popup is presented on the page.

redirectUrl.description: HTTP or HTTPS URL for successful signups. Pass an empty string to switch back to the confirmation message.

resubscribeBehavior.description: What happens when a contact who unsubscribed from all email submits this popup again. reactivate (the default) resubscribes them and restores the popup's lists; double_opt_in sends a confirmation email first and resubscribes them when they confirm. Workspace double opt-in always requires confirmation. duplicateStrategy never changes subscription status.

reward.description: Scratch-to-reveal reward. When enabled the popup opens on a scratch card: the visitor scratches (or taps "Tap to reveal") to see a public teaser, clicks Claim, enters their email, and only then sees the reward. { "enabled": true, "value": "10% off your first order" (required when enabled, max 120, private), "code": "WELCOME10" (optional, letters/numbers/-/_, max 64, private), "heading": "Try your luck", "subheading": "Scratch below to see what you win", "teaserEyebrow": "You've got a", "teaser": "Mystery discount", "claimText": "Claim", "coverText": "Scratch here", "coverStyle": "gold" | "silver" | "rose-gold" | "holographic" | "accent" | "custom", "coverColor": "#rrggbb" (used by custom), "coverTextColor": "#rrggbb" | null, "coverPattern": "sheen" | "sparkle" | "plain", "coverImageUrl": "https://..." | null (needs CORS headers, otherwise the foil shows), "prizeBackgroundColor": "#rrggbb" | null, "prizeTextColor": "#rrggbb" | null, "cardRadius": 0-32 }. value and code never appear in the embed script; a successful submit returns them and saves them on the subscriber as the `discount` attribute, so welcome emails can use {{discount.value}} and {{discount.code}} (a create-discount step in the same sequence takes precedence). A `discount` attribute the contact already has from another source is never overwritten. Rejected while enabled: an empty value, a redirect after submission (send redirectUrl ""), the floating-bar presentation, and form fields named `discount`. Merged into the current reward.

schedule.description: Optional run window as ISO 8601 timestamps: { "startsAt": "2026-09-01T00:00:00Z", "endsAt": "2026-09-08T00:00:00Z" }. Use null on either key to clear it. Merged into the current schedule.

status.description: Set to published to make the popup live, or draft to stop it showing while keeping it and its stats. The embed script stays valid either way.

successMessage.description: New confirmation message on the success screen.

tagIds.description: Replacement tag IDs applied to every signup. Pass an empty array to clear tags.

targeting.description: Where the popup may show. { "domains": ["shop.example.com"], "paths": ["/pricing"], "excludedPaths": ["/checkout"], "device": "all" | "desktop" | "mobile" }. Empty arrays mean no restriction. Merged into the current targeting.

theme.description: Visual theme overrides merged into the current theme. Any subset of: accentColor, backgroundColor, textColor, mutedTextColor, cardColor, borderColor (all #rrggbb), borderRadius (0-32), headingFontFamily, bodyFontFamily, density (compact | balanced | spacious).

trigger.description: When the popup opens. { "type": "delay" | "scroll" | "exit-intent" | "click" | "manual", "delaySeconds": 0-3600, "scrollPercent": 1-100, "clickSelector": "#join" }. Only the key each type uses matters: delay reads delaySeconds, scroll reads scrollPercent, and click requires a clickSelector CSS selector. Merged into the current trigger, so patching one key keeps the rest.

visual.description: Media panel and urgency treatment: { "style": "none" | "accent" | "header" | "rail" | "image" | "countdown", "placement": "top" | "left" | "center" | "right", "imageUrl": "https://...", "imageAlt": "...", "countdownMinutes": 1-10080 }. Use style "image" with an imageUrl for a product panel, or "countdown" with countdownMinutes for a deadline. Style "image" requires an https imageUrl - without one the popup renders the accent rail instead of the split layout, so setting it without an image is rejected. Merged into the current visual.

name: update_popup

outputSchema.description: Structured content returned by the `update_popup` MCP tool.

embed.description: Script URL plus HTML, React, WordPress, and Shopify snippets (published popups only).

items.description: Fallback array wrapper used only when a tool returns a bare array.

message.description: Human-readable status, confirmation, or next-step message.

popup.description: The saved popup record returned by Sequenzy.

value.description: Fallback object wrapper used only when a tool returns a non-object value.

warnings.description: Non-fatal cautions about content, permissions, or follow-up actions.
